title: Bulgur Pilaf with Cremini Mushrooms and Parsley
summary: Nutty bulgur is simmered with earthy porcini and cremini mushrooms for a savoury, herb-flecked pilaf that makes a hearty side or light main.

ingredients.item: dried porcini, rinsed and finely chopped
fine sea salt or table salt
cremini mushrooms, trimmed and quartered (halved if small)
vegetable stock (check stock label for celery)

steps.title: Soften
steps.text: Warm 2 tbsp olive oil in a large saucepan on medium and cook the finely chopped onion with 7 g chopped dried porcini and ¼ tsp salt until soft, about 5 minutes.

steps.title: Brown
steps.text: Add 225 g quartered cremini mushrooms, cover and cook on medium-high until they release their liquid and start to brown, about 4 minutes, then stir in the chopped garlic for 30 seconds.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Stir in 175 g rinsed bulgur, 180 ml stock, 180 ml water and 1 tsp soy sauce, bring to a simmer, then cover and cook on low until tender, 16-18 minutes.

steps.title: Rest
steps.text: Take off the heat, slide a folded tea towel under the lid and leave to rest for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Fluff with a fork, fold in 4 tbsp chopped parsley, season with ¼ tsp pepper and serve.

tips: Rinse the bulgur first to wash away starchy dust and keep the grains separate.
Let the covered pan rest under a tea towel after cooking so the steam finishes softening the grains evenly.
Check the stock label if avoiding celery, as some vegetable stocks include it.
storage: Keep in a covered container in the fridge for up to 3 days and reheat gently with a splash of water. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
